paper.title: Learning Multimodal Bipedal Locomotion and Implicit Transitions: A Versatile Policy Approach
paper.source_version: arXiv v2 (2023-08-12); PDF SHA-256 2706df707af15cc3857935d2f8ba10fa24671fc9dda7b6e093766239ddc8b97b; TeX archive SHA-256 207ed8b18493e4fe560fe041dc268483cf629349bb1d5adb5d922f7fea4d1b91

decision_relevance.why_admitted: Direct precursor to OGMP: it turns rough reference clips into latent mode commands, samples ordered mode switches to learn implicit transitions, and composes open-loop mode plans. It supplies concrete reference, reward, and evaluation hypotheses while exposing a strict fixed-trainer boundary.
not_evidence_for: An explicit state-feedback oracle or branching state machine
A composed or certified transition reference
A fixed-trainer comparison isolating only reference composition or task reward
Hardware transfer, impact safety, or dynamics feasibility of rough references
RL-Sculptor implementation of the paper mechanism
Independent objective evaluation: Table II uses normalized returns linked to the training reward

mechanisms.name: Rough reference library
mechanisms.description: User keyframes define base position and orientation; an optional binary contact sequence per leg distinguishes contact patterns. No actuated-joint reference is required, and the reference need not be kinematically or dynamically feasible.

mechanisms.name: Whole-clip latent mode encoder
mechanisms.description: An LSTM autoencoder maps an entire variable-length reference trajectory to one state-agnostic latent point before policy training, using L2 reconstruction loss.

mechanisms.name: Mode- and clock-conditioned multimodal policy
mechanisms.description: One PPO policy receives proprioception, a two-component phase clock, and the current latent mode; it outputs ten motor targets converted to clipped torques by fixed PD gains.

mechanisms.name: Rough-reference tracking reward
mechanisms.description: A weighted sum of exponential penalties tracks base position, base orientation, and optionally the two-leg contact state.

mechanisms.name: Return-adaptive mode and transition sampler
mechanisms.description: Initial modes are drawn from a marginal distribution derived from per-mode returns; final modes are drawn conditionally from an ordered-pair return matrix. Lower-return modes and transitions receive higher probability, with history retention and a nonzero sampling floor.

mechanisms.name: Implicit transition learning
mechanisms.description: The command changes discretely from an initial to a final latent mode during a rollout. The single policy, not an explicit transition trajectory or switched controller, must produce the intermediate maneuver.

mechanisms.name: Open-loop mode planner
mechanisms.description: A zero-order spline of mode IDs is optimized with tabular Q-learning. Knot index is the planner state and mode index the action; Monte Carlo rollouts maximize a goal-position reward. The resulting schedule has no terrain or robot-state feedback.

failure_modes.name: Mode aliasing
failure_modes.description: The one-hot behavior-encoding baseline produced indistinguishable walk and leap base-height profiles; the paper attributes separation under learned encodings to informative latent features as a hypothesis.

failure_modes.name: Mode collapse under uniform sampling
failure_modes.description: The uniformly sampled nine-mode policy failed the leap-left mode while adaptive sampling tracked all modes more consistently.

failure_modes.name: Transition collapse under uniform sampling
failure_modes.description: Uniform ordered-pair sampling reached a local optimum that succeeded on a subset of transitions and did not recover.

failure_modes.name: Out-of-distribution states under unimodal switching
failure_modes.description: Discrete walk-to-launch policy switching failed because the launch policy had not encountered the transition states.

failure_modes.name: Open-loop planner blindness
failure_modes.description: The mode planner receives neither exteroceptive terrain feedback nor proprioceptive robot state, so it cannot branch or replan from observed execution error.

failure_modes.name: Coarse and saturating speed control
failure_modes.description: The mode-conditioned policy lacks granular velocity control. Clock-rate modulation doubled leap speed from 0.5 to 1.0 m/s at 2× and saturated near 1.2 m/s at 3×.

failure_modes.name: Simulation and motion-quality evidence gap
failure_modes.description: Hardware transfer was not a focus, and reward shaping for high-impact or jittery motion was absent. The results do not certify hardware feasibility or safety.

failure_modes.name: Reward-linked primary metric
failure_modes.description: Table II's normalized mean return aggregates the training reward, so it is not an objective metric independent of the generated or selected reward. This is a harness evidence boundary, not a paper error.

failure_modes.name: Unversioned code dependencies
failure_modes.description: The paper links an external LSTM autoencoder and an external PPO implementation without commit hashes, and no paper-specific implementation artifact is identified in the primary record.

evaluation.name: Adaptive versus uniform sampling
evaluation.description: For pi1 and pi2, adaptive sampling increased the reported normalized mean returns across both modes and directed transitions relative to uniform sampling; the transition variance for pi2 remained large.

evaluation.name: Learned latent versus one-hot commands
evaluation.description: The reported qualitative/base-height comparison shows distinct walk and leap profiles for learned encodings and aliased profiles for one-hot commands; the causal feature explanation is explicitly framed as a hypothesis.

evaluation.name: Single multimodal policy versus switched unimodal policies
evaluation.description: Four individually successful unimodal policies failed when switched on the parkour sequence, whereas the multimodal policy executed walk-to-launch, launch-to-leap, and leap-to-idle transitions.

evaluation.name: Optional contact-reference test
evaluation.description: With the same constant-height base reference, in-phase versus alternating leg-contact schedules produced hop versus walk behavior in pi3.

evaluation.name: Open-loop mode-planning tasks
evaluation.description: Three simulated reach-goal tasks with a gap, plateau, or gap-plus-block were solved by selecting the best of parallel Q-learning/Monte Carlo searches; reported solve times were approximately three minutes.

evidence.locator: Header and Abstract; arXiv v2 dated 12 Aug 2023
evidence.claim: The exact source version names Lokesh Krishna and Quan Nguyen and states the rough-reference, adaptive-sampling, implicit-transition, and open-loop-planning scope.
References are linear interpolations of base-pose keyframes with optional per-leg contact sequences; they need not be feasible and omit joint trajectories.

evidence.locator: Section II-B, Equation 1 and final paragraph
evidence.claim: An entire reference trajectory is encoded to one latent vector by an LSTM autoencoder with one 32-neuron hidden layer; the paper links sequitur without a commit.
The policy observes 31-D state, two-component phase clock, and latent mode; n_m=4 is reported as minimally sufficient; ten motor targets use Kp=30, Kd=0.5, and 30 Nm clipping.
The reward sums exponential base-position, base-orientation, and contact-state tracking terms with sensitivities [5,5,2].
Sampling probabilities are derived from per-mode and conditional transition returns, favor poor performers; epsilon=0.2 and gamma values 0.2, 0.4, and 0.8 are reported.
The algorithm samples initial/final modes, switches at phase 0.25, 0.5, or 0.75 in clip 0 or 1, rolls out the single policy, updates PPO, and updates mode/pair return records.

evidence.locator: Section II-E, Equation 4 and final paragraph
evidence.claim: The zero-order mode plan is optimized by tabular Q-learning and Monte Carlo rollouts; the planner has neither terrain nor robot-state feedback and emits only a time-dependent open-loop plan.

evidence.locator: Table I and Section III opening paragraph
evidence.claim: The three policy configurations use 4 or 9 modes, 16 or 81 ordered transitions, stated reward weights, MuJoCo, two-day training, eight CPU workers, and an unpinned external PPO repository.
Adaptive sampling reports higher normalized mean returns than uniform sampling across modes and transitions for pi1 and pi2, with the exact means and deviations extracted here.

evidence.locator: Section III-A, Choice of behavior encoding and Choice of mode sampling
evidence.claim: The one-hot baseline aliases walk and leap, while uniform sampling collapses on leap-left; the authors state the latent-feature explanation as a hypothesis.

evidence.locator: Section III-A, Trained with and without contact sequence and Frequency of motion in modes
evidence.claim: Contact timing distinguishes hop from walk under the same base reference; clock-rate scaling changes leap speed but saturates.
Separately switched unimodal policies fail from transition-state distribution shift; the multimodal policy executes implicit transitions, and adaptive pair sampling reduces transition collapse.
The paper reports open-loop plan knots, periods, approximately three-minute solve times, and terrain dimensions for gap, plateau, and block tasks.
Hardware transfer was not a focus, extensive reward shaping for high-impact/jittery motion was absent, and feedback-aware planning was left to future work.
The paper was published in the 2023 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems under DOI 10.1109/IROS55552.2023.10342398.

OGMP explicitly cites this paper as [15], reuses its learned LSTM latent-mode and phase-clock lineage, and adds task-vital parameterized modes, receding-horizon oracle trajectories, and oracle-neighborhood state constraints.
